summary: The preregistered treatment model cannot be executed by the locked tesseract.js runtime. The compatibility gate failed closed before either arm produced data, exactly as preregistered. No comparison result exists.

rootCause.finding: Every LSTM-only Tesseract WASM core shipped by tesseract.js-core 7.0.0 is integer-only. Running a float (tessdata_best) model under one aborts on a missing float dot-product symbol.
rootCause.corroboration: tesseract.js's own node worker defaults lstmOnly language data to the '4.0.0_best_int' (integer-quantized) dataset, which is consistent with the LSTM-only cores supporting integer weights only.
rootCause.coreSelection: src/worker-script/node/getCore.js ignores the caller's corePath and selects a core by runtime SIMD feature detection. On this machine relaxedSimd=true, so tesseract-core-relaxedsimd-lstm was loaded.
rootCause.floatCapableCores: The float-capable full cores (tesseract-core, tesseract-core-simd, tesseract-core-relaxedsimd) are selected only when OEM is not DEFAULT/LSTM_ONLY, i.e. for the legacy-capable modes. Neither model in this experiment carries legacy components, so those OEM values cannot initialize either.

probeMethod.image: synthetic 420x120 PNG rendered from an SVG containing the single word SYNTHETIC
probeMethod.note: Diagnostic only. A synthetic image was used specifically so that characterising the blocker could not touch corpus crops or contaminate the frozen protocol.
probeMethod.isolation: each configuration run in its own process, because tesseract.js caches the loaded core at module scope

probeMatrix.verdict: WORKS — establishes the runtime and probe are sound; the failure below is specific to the float model, not the environment
FAILS — aborts on the missing float dot-product symbol inside the frozen run; hangs without completing in the isolated probe
NOT ESTABLISHED — the probe hung and was terminated after a bounded wait; this path is neither confirmed working nor confirmed broken

whatWasNotDone.coreSubstitution: Forcing a float-capable core would change the WASM core build, a second dimension the preregistration holds fixed. Not done.
whatWasNotDone.oemChange: Changing OEM would be a second dimension and is impossible against models with no legacy components. Not done.
whatWasNotDone.treatmentSubstitution: Swapping in a different, weaker treatment after the gate failed would be post-hoc treatment substitution. Not done.
whatWasNotDone.secondArm: Adding a second traineddata/config arm is forbidden. Not done.
whatWasNotDone.rationale: The preregistration fixed one variable and specified that the run fails closed if the gate fails. It failed closed. Reporting a blocker is the correct outcome; improvising a runnable variant would have produced a result the design did not authorise.

followUpPath.status: requires a separate preregistration; not authorised by this package
followUpPath.option: Run the float model under a float-capable full core, which necessarily changes two dimensions relative to today's control (traineddata variant AND WASM core build). A clean design would therefore need either a three-arm decomposition or an explicit statement that the core build is part of the treatment definition.
followUpPath.openQuestion: Whether tesseract.js 7.0.0 can pair a float LSTM model with a full core in Node at all was not established here — the bounded probe hung rather than answering.
followUpPath.alternative: Vendor the integer-quantized variant of a different official model, which would stay inside the integer-only core constraint, if any such variant is genuinely stronger than the current one.
